summary: Mount Kearsarge Lookout (also listed as Kearsarge South) in Merrimack County, NH; station 1909, tower announced 1924, restored 2012, cabs replaced 2019; NHLR-registered 2002; standing.

facts.design: Tower with legs, cross bracing and a cabin on girders (per the 2012 restoration list); no height in these sources
facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

events.note: Station built on Mt. Kearsarge in the fall of 1909 by the state forestry commission
July 17, 1910 fire in pine slash near the Kearsarge post office, spotted by the Mt. Kearsarge watchman and put out after four hours
September 1924 notice: the state forestry department was erecting four new lookout towers, one on Mount Kearsarge; not confirmed as the present structure
Restoration by Saco Ranger District personnel (WMNF staff per a second account); tower legs, cabin girders, fascia boards and cross bracing replaced; materials flown in by helicopter
Tower cabs replaced and other work done on the Mt. Kearsarge tower, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association's 2019 New Hampshire report; the report does not name who did the work

corrections.why: No source read gives a height. The Register gives only elevation. 81.7 m is about 268 ft, which no source read supports for this small summit tower. The 1924 notice in the Forest Lookouts page mentions a tower but gives no height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 2,937 ft (895 m), matching the record. The Forest Lookouts page gives a 3,268 ft summit for the 2012 work. The Register figure is kept.
The 1909 station and the September 1924 notice both point to a lookout on the mountain. The Register gives no build date, and no source read says which structure stands today.

notes_for_editor: Record gaps: no height and no access rule found. Access was left out because no source read gives a visit or climbing rule, so the story asks visitors to check with the state. The FFLA report is titled 'FFLA New Hampshire Chapter Report for 2019' in its text, so the 2019 year is confirmed. The record's 'state replaced the cab' is not in the report; see corrections. The 81.7 m height in the record looks like an error and should be checked before publishing. The fire record is for the mountain station and watchman, not necessarily this structure. Search results mentioned a 27-foot 1924 steel tower and a 1953-54 larger cab; I could not read those pages in the session, so they are not used. One search snippet also said a 2019 date was not found; the FFLA 2019 report does mention cab work, so that snippet was wrong.
